tweet.text:
Nex-N2.5 Mini is an open-weight 35B MoE model built for local inference and visually grounded computer-use workflows.**

With a compatible agent runtime, Computer Use starts with a goal—not click-by-click instructions. Tell it to open a page, find the latest product, and summarize the results in a table, and it can work through the execution loop using visual feedback and tools.

**Same-prompt test: Nex-N2.5 Mini vs. Qwen3.5-35B-A3B**

I gave both models the same task:

“Open this webpage, extract the table, and save it as Markdown.”

In this run, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B generated a plausible script, but referenced an API endpoint that was not available in the test environment. The code looked convincing, but it did not complete the task.

Nex-N2.5 Mini opened the browser, located the table, extracted the data, and saved the Markdown file. It also caught a malformed row, checked the output, reran the extraction, and delivered a clean result without human intervention.

**Task completion in this test:**

- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B: 0/1
- Nex-N2.5 Mini: 1/1
- Human interventions required by Nex: 0

This is a single-run case study, not a general benchmark. But in this test, Qwen produced better-looking prose; Nex actually delivered the requested artifact.

**For developers: what it actually takes to run Mini**

The official BF16 checkpoint is approximately 70.2GB, and the reference deployment uses a single node with 2×H100 GPUs.

But the community has already produced smaller local conversions:

- GGUF Q4_K_M: approximately 21.17GB
- MLX 4-bit: approximately 19.53GB

A 24GB GPU may be able to run the Q4_K_M build with a conservative context length and careful memory settings or partial CPU offloading. It is not a blanket guarantee: the runtime, KV cache, and optional ~0.9GB vision projector also consume memory.

The MLX 4-bit conversion runs on Apple Silicon, but the current release contains text-generation weights only and does not include a vision projector. It is suitable for local text, coding, and tool-use experiments—not the full visual Computer Use workflow shown above.

NVIDIA users can load the GGUF build with a current llama.cpp-compatible runtime or LM Studio. For screen understanding, the vision projector and compatible multimodal and tool-calling support are also required.

The Nex-N2.5 Mini and Pro are both available through OpenRouter for free for a limited time.

You don’t need to wait for local Pro weights to start building. Run Mini today, validate your workflow, and evaluate Pro through OpenRouter. 

🔗 Mini and Pro on OpenRouter:  
https://openrouter.ai/nex-agi

🔗 Official Mini weights:  
https://huggingface.co/nex-agi/Nex-N2.5-mini

🔗 Community GGUF:  
https://huggingface.co/abenzerps/Nex-N2.5-mini-GGUF

🔗 Community MLX 4-bit:  
https://huggingface.co/abenzerps/Nex-N2.5-mini-MLX-4bit

#NexN25 #ComputerUse #LocalAI #AIAgents
